frame: Z is the anatomical symmetry axis; +Z points out through the corneal apex. Origin is halfway between exterior axial endpoints, not a measured rotation center.

literature_inputs.locator: Table 1 (p. 571): width, base radius, height, posterior curvature. Table 2 (p. 574): external axial endpoint, anterior radius and retinal endpoints.

assumptions: Rotational symmetry: repeat the measured nasotemporal diameter in both transverse axes.
Use the cornea base radius as a circular limbus radius and cornea height as apex-to-limbus-plane sag.
Close the posterior exterior with a spheroid; do not fit the reported posterior pole curvature.
Join cap and body position-continuously with a visible slope change; no invented smoothing fillet.
The local axis is not a calibrated visual axis; no skull pose or eye rotation center is inferred.
